reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) discusses general ATF coating strategies and mentions CrAl coatings and AlTiCrNiTa coatings for oxidation resistance, but provides no specific data on Al segregation, formation of a continuous Al2O3 interlayer at the Cr–Zr interface, or its effect on interdiffusion kinetics. The key premises about the mechanism and performance boundaries are therefore unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Al addition to Cr coating leads to Al segregation at the Cr–Zr interface
Segregated Al forms a continuous nanocrystalline Al2O3 or mixed Cr2O3–Al2O3 interlayer upon oxidation
This oxide interlayer impedes Cr–Zr interdiffusion by reducing vacancy formation and atomic mobility
The Al-doped coating maintains oxidation protection in subcritical water (~320 °C) and high-temperature steam (~1200 °C)
The mechanism is effective with 5–10 at.% Al incorporated via co-sputtering
